hello.note: One syllable; to strangers use Dzień dobry.

slang.note: Casual peer greeting; skip with elders or strangers.

good_morning.note: Also the daytime hello; dz sounds like English j.

goodbye.note: dz here is the ds in 'kids', not a plain z.

slang.note: Clipped from na razie; friends and peers only.

how_are_you.note: ś is a soft, hissy sh. Formal: Jak się pan ma? (pahn mah).

slang.note: Everyday casual check-in; fine among friends.

thank_you.note: ę is nasal: hum the n of 'jen' through the nose.

excuse_me.note: prze comes out 'psheh'; it doubles as 'sorry'.

sorry.note: 'I'm very sorry'; dz sounds like j; Przepraszam OK too.

slang.note: Casual, upbeat; fine with friends or strangers.

delicious.note: y is the short i of 'bit', so PISH, not 'peesh'.

slang.note: Playful, kid-friendly; fine with anyone at the table.
Cute, casual toast; friends and family.
